memory_update.text: Primary public chokepoint candidates for staples input/cold-chain/packaging node: LINE, COLD, BALL, GPK, IFF.

Cold-chain infrastructure appears to have the cleanest direct bottleneck mapping because USDA reports finite U.S. refrigerated capacity, while LINE and COLD provide concentrated public-market exposure to temperature-controlled warehouse networks.

Packaging candidates should be split by substrate: BALL for aluminum beverage packaging and GPK for paperboard food/beverage/foodservice packaging. Key falsification metrics are volume weakness, excess capacity, and inability to pass through aluminum/fiber/energy costs.

Protein processors, glass packaging, plastic films, refrigeration equipment, and wholesale grocery distribution were not fully covered due to the five-candidate limit; next pass should test TSN, HRL, PPC, OI, AMCR, CCK, PKG, USFD, SYY, PFGC, UNFI, CARR, and TT for node relevance.

Ingredient universe may require a separate pass comparing IFF, INGR, ADM, BG, DAR, and FMC-like food/ag inputs; current inclusion of IFF is based on specialty formulation and shelf-life relevance rather than proven 2026 pricing power.

The strongest chokepoint mappings in this pass are temperature-controlled warehouse capacity, aluminum beverage packaging, paperboard packaging for CPG/foodservice, and specialty food ingredients that affect taste, texture, preservation, and shelf life.
